title: Student App and Journey Integration
problemSolved: Students navigate a fragmented digital estate with no single useful place to start their day, and King’s does not yet have a coherent student-facing product and reusable app platform through which essential information, services and deeper digital journeys can be brought together.
whatChanges: King’s uses 2026/27 as a discovery-led mobilisation year for the Digital Student Experience Hub, combining broad discovery of the wider student digital estate, priority journeys, information architecture, ownership and readiness with deliberately focused implementation. The Hub will be a bespoke aggregation, orchestration and intelligence layer over authoritative institutional systems rather than a wholesale replatforming of them. King’s Edge is the first substantive native product domain. The current hypothesis for the September 2027 first live release combines the shared student home and King’s Edge with light-touch access to timetabling, KEATS and a designed gateway into the separately delivered student-enquiry-management capability; discovery may refine that mix. Evidence from delivery, broad discovery and live use then determines where the Hub should deepen next.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Aligned the Strategic Initiative and mobilisation-plan direction: Year One discovery will be broad while implementation remains focused; July 2027 is the Year One mobilisation and launch-readiness point and September 2027 the first live institutional Hub release; King’s Edge is the fixed first deep native domain, while timetable, KEATS and the student-enquiry gateway are the current first-release hypotheses subject to discovery; the Hub owns the student-facing gateway to enquiry management, not the underlying enquiry-management service; Mark Peace leads mobilisation and maturation, with enduring student-facing product ownership expected to transition into SED and technical/platform ownership remaining with Digital and IT; initial Year One governance can remain light-touch through existing routes with deliberate assurance, but dedicated cross-institution governance is required before deeper mobilisation; the working strategic investment envelope is £3m over three years, with the £291k Year One baseline retained and recurrent post-mobilisation costs to be evidenced; by the end of the three-year mobilisation the Hub should be a broad, established institutional product with a substantial range of integrated journeys and some parallel entry points rationalised, while retaining an ongoing product roadmap.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Confirmed that AI is an enabling capability that should be introduced progressively rather than the organising principle of the Hub. Confirmed rationalisation of the student-facing digital estate as an explicit programme objective, with retirement or consolidation only where replacement functionality and service continuity are proven. Rationalisation will be measured through the proportion of priority journeys coherently accessible through the Hub and demonstrated reduction of redundant or competing entry points, rather than an arbitrary 50% portal-count target.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Confirmed the formal initiative name as Digital Student Experience Hub, retaining digital front door as a descriptive phrase. Confirmed Student Systems and Data as a critical dependency for the mature Hub and deeper integrated journeys, but not a gating dependency for the focused September 2027 first release. Confirmed Hannah Robinson as accountable owner for 4.1.1 Student Relationship and CRM Foundation, which remains within 4.1 for strategic coherence while continuing through its existing in-flight delivery route.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Confirmed that the Digital Student Experience Hub itself will be a bespoke solution at the aggregation, orchestration and intelligence layer. It will create a bespoke student-facing experience over authoritative institutional systems and selectively integrate their data and functionality, without implying wholesale replatforming or replacement of the underlying source systems.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Confirmed that the five Strategic Initiative work packages are a strategic reporting lens across the Digital Student Experience Hub rather than a one-to-one copy of repository deliverables. Refined the five packages as Programme Governance, Ownership and Assurance; Student Journey, Service and Information Discovery & Design; Digital Estate, Architecture and Integration Foundations; Bespoke Hub Product and Iterative Delivery; and Adoption, Rationalisation and Continuous Product Development. Repository deliverables may contribute to multiple work packages and should remain structured around executable delivery responsibility.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Confirmed the initiative’s portfolio position as Education-owned, with Digital and IT as a core delivery partner and technical/platform owner. Mobilisation accountability remains with Mark Peace, with enduring student-facing product ownership expected to transition into SED as the Hub enters business as usual.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Removed Net Promoter Score as a proposed Hub success measure. The programme will instead establish baseline measures from the first live release for successful completion of priority student journeys and perceived ease of use, then set evidence-based improvement targets from live data rather than applying an arbitrary NPS threshold.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Removed the previously suggested CampusM/UCL Go-style interim app option. The programme will not introduce a separate interim app layer: the King’s Edge replatform and first-release work should contribute directly to the bespoke Digital Student Experience Hub foundations so investment strengthens the intended long-term product rather than creating another transitional destination.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Reframed the remaining operational percentage OKRs as evidence-led outcome measures. Year One and the first live release will establish credible baselines for active use, duplicated or conflicting content, first-time journey success, personalisation reach and engagement with nudges; quantified improvement targets will then be set from discovery and live evidence rather than retaining unsupported headline percentages.

decisionLog.forum: Student Experience Hub strategic alignment review
decisionLog.outcome: Final consolidation confirmed the dependency model: Student Systems and Data is critical to the mature Hub but does not gate September 2027; the Student Relationship and CRM Foundation is critical to the depth of the enquiry journey but does not gate the first release; and the King’s Edge replatform proceeds independently of completion of 1.2 while aligning the specific authoritative-data and interface requirements it needs. The first release can therefore remain focused and supportable while deeper journeys are sequenced according to service, data, API and CRM readiness.
